look_here_first: FIRST use a hand lens on upper flowering stems, peduncles and outer phyllary faces for stalked glandular hairs; check short oblong, often rough/aromatic leaves and a low bushy rhizomatous habit. Do not identify solely from purple rays or smell.

best_field_traits: Perennial, often low and densely branched, spreading by rhizomes.
Short oblong to linear-oblong leaves, often rough and aromatic when handled; compare lower and upper leaves.
Stalked glandular hairs on upper stems, peduncles and phyllary faces are high-value ID features.
Heads with ray and disc florets; involucres roughly (5-)7-9 mm in FNA treatment; verify with scale and glands.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. praealtum usually tall, willow-leaved and broadly paniculate; S. patens has rougher clasping upper leaves and usually nonglandular-hairy stems; S. ericoides has very small stiff narrow leaves and much smaller heads. For S. oblongifolium inspect stalked glands on peduncles and phyllaries, not ray color alone.
